evals.prompt: csvsum/ has no README yet. Write csvsum/README.md for someone who has never seen the tool: what it does, what they need installed, and a quick start they can copy and paste that shows the output they should get.
evals.expected_output: A README with a one-sentence lead, the Python requirement taken from pyproject.toml (3.10 or later), a quick start run from csvsum/ against data/sales.csv whose Expected output block matches the real output (for example 852.75 for the revenue column), all documented commands passing check_doc_commands.py, and no broken links.

assertions.text: Every documented command in README.md runs from csvsum/ and at least one has its expected output shown and matching (check_doc_commands.py).
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_doc_commands.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_doc_commands.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_doc_commands.py"; O=$(python3 "$T" csvsum/README.md --cwd csvsum --timeout 30 2>&1); s=$?; echo "$O"; [ $s -eq 0 ] && echo "$O" | grep -q "^ok " && echo "$O" | grep -q "output matches"

assertions.text: README.md states the Python requirement from pyproject.toml (3.10).
README.md has no broken relative links or anchors (check_links.py).
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_links.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_links.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/check_links.py"; python3 "$T" csvsum/README.md

evals.prompt: Just rewrap wrap-docs/docs/guide.markdown so prose lines are at most 80 characters. Don't change anything else.
evals.expected_output: Prose and list items rewrapped at 80 columns; every word, the URL, and the code block unchanged (the long docker command stays on one line), proved with same_words.py.

assertions.text: same_words.py finds the same words, URLs, and code lines as the original file.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/same_words.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "same_words.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/document-codebases/scripts/same_words.py"; python3 "$T" "$R/skills/document-codebases/evals/files/wrap-docs/docs/guide.markdown" wrap-docs/docs/guide.markdown

assertions.text: Every line outside fenced code blocks is at most 80 characters, except a line holding only an unbreakable link.
assertions.check:
python3 - wrap-docs/docs/guide.markdown <<'PY'
import re, sys
fence, bad = False, []
for n, line in enumerate(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines(), 1):
    if line.lstrip().startswith('```'):
        fence = not fence
        continue
    if not fence and len(line) > 80 and not re.fullmatch(r'\s*(?:[-*]\s+)?\S*\]\(\S+\)\S*', line):
        bad.append((n, len(line)))
print(bad)
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
PY

evals.prompt: Add an entry for the new --precision flag to csvsum-release/CHANGELOG.md.
evals.expected_output: Near miss (changelog, not general docs): an Added entry for --precision under [Unreleased], worded for users; README.md and the program unchanged.

assertions.check:
python3 - csvsum-release/CHANGELOG.md <<'PY'
import sys
text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8').read()
start = text.find('## [Unreleased]'); end = text.find('## [0.3.0]')
sys.exit(0 if 0 <= start < end and '--precision' in text[start:end] else 1)
PY
